gods.name: Lord Brahma
gods.title: The Creator
gods.desc: Brahma is the creator god, part of the Trimurti, and is depicted with four faces.
gods.details: He is associated with wisdom and the Vedas, and his consort is Saraswati, goddess of knowledge.

gods.name: Lord Vishnu
gods.title: The Preserver
gods.desc: Vishnu is the preserver and protector of the universe, often shown with blue skin and four arms.
gods.details: He is known for his ten avatars, including Rama and Krishna, and is always depicted with a conch, discus, mace, and lotus.

gods.name: Lord Shiva
gods.title: The Destroyer
gods.desc: Shiva, the destroyer and transformer, is depicted with a trident, crescent moon, and the river Ganga flowing from his hair.
gods.details: He is the master of meditation and yoga, and his consort is Parvati. His vahana (vehicle) is the bull Nandi.

gods.name: Lakshmi
gods.title: Goddess of Wealth
gods.desc: Lakshmi is the goddess of wealth, fortune, and prosperity, often shown with gold coins and lotuses.
gods.details: She is the consort of Vishnu and is worshipped especially during Diwali for prosperity and good luck.

mantra.sanskrit: ॐ श्रीं ह्रीं श्रीं कमले कमलालये प्रसीद
mantra.english: Om Shreem Hreem Shreem Kamale Kamalalaye Praseed

gods.name: Saraswati
gods.title: Goddess of Knowledge
gods.desc: Saraswati is the goddess of wisdom, music, and learning, depicted with a veena and a swan.
gods.details: She is the consort of Brahma and is worshipped by students and artists for wisdom and creativity.

gods.name: Parvati
gods.title: Mother Goddess
gods.desc: Parvati is the goddess of power, harmony, and devotion, wife of Shiva and mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya.
gods.details: She is also worshipped as Durga and Kali in her fierce forms.

gods.name: Durga
gods.title: Goddess of Power
gods.desc: Durga is the fierce form of Parvati, symbolizing strength and protection, often shown riding a lion or tiger.
gods.details: She is celebrated during Navratri and is known for slaying the buffalo demon Mahishasura.

gods.name: Kali
gods.title: Goddess of Time & Change
gods.desc: Kali is the goddess of destruction and transformation, depicted with dark skin and a garland of skulls.
gods.details: She is a fierce form of Parvati, representing the power of time and change, and is worshipped for protection from evil.

gods.name: Ganesha
gods.title: Remover of Obstacles
gods.desc: Ganesha, the elephant-headed god, is the remover of obstacles and patron of arts and sciences.
gods.details: He is the son of Shiva and Parvati, and is worshipped at the start of new ventures for good fortune.

gods.name: Hanuman
gods.title: Monkey God
gods.desc: Hanuman is the devoted servant of Rama, symbolizing strength, devotion, and courage.
gods.details: He is a central figure in the Ramayana, known for his loyalty, bravery, and ability to change form at will.

gods.name: Rama
gods.title: Seventh Avatar of Vishnu
gods.desc: Rama, the hero of the Ramayana, is the embodiment of virtue, courage, and devotion.
gods.details: He is the ideal king and husband, and his story is celebrated during the festival of Diwali.

gods.name: Krishna
gods.title: Eighth Avatar of Vishnu
gods.desc: Krishna is worshipped as the god of compassion, tenderness, and love, and is a central figure in the Mahabharata.
gods.details: He is known for his childhood pranks, the Bhagavad Gita, and the festival of Janmashtami.

gods.name: Skanda
gods.title: God of War
gods.desc: Skanda, also known as Kartikeya or Murugan, is the god of war and the son of Shiva and Parvati.
gods.details: He is especially popular in South India and is depicted riding a peacock and holding a spear.

gods.name: Sita
gods.title: Wife of Rama
gods.desc: Sita is the incarnation of Lakshmi and the devoted wife of Rama, known for her purity and courage.
gods.details: She is a central character in the Ramayana and is revered as the ideal woman and wife.

asuras.name: Hiranyaksha
asuras.title: The Golden-Eyed Demon
asuras.desc: A mighty Daitya who dragged the Earth into the cosmic ocean.
asuras.details: He was slain by Lord Vishnu in his Varaha (boar) avatar after a thousand-year battle to restore the Earth to its rightful place.

asuras.name: Hiranyakashipu
asuras.title: Enemy of Devotion
asuras.desc: A tyrannical Asura king who demanded to be worshipped as God.
asuras.details: Granted a boon of near-immortality by Brahma, he tormented his son Prahlada. He was brutally slain by Lord Vishnu's Narasimha avatar at twilight.

asuras.name: Bhasmasura
asuras.title: The Ash Demon
asuras.desc: An Asura granted the power to turn anyone to ashes by touching their head.
asuras.details: He attempted to use this boon on Lord Shiva himself. He was ultimately tricked by Vishnu in the form of Mohini into touching his own head, reducing himself to ash.

mantra.english: I shall turn all to ash!

asuras.name: Alakshmi
asuras.title: Goddess of Misfortune
asuras.desc: The shadow sister of Lakshmi, representing grief, jealousy, and poverty.
asuras.details: She arose during the churning of the cosmic ocean (Samudra Manthan) just before Lakshmi, embodying the struggles and misfortunes of the material world.

mantra.english: Alakshmir Nashaya (Prayer to ward her off)

asuras.name: Kumbhakarna
asuras.title: The Slumbering Giant
asuras.desc: The colossal brother of Ravana known for his endless sleep and immense appetite.
asuras.details: Despite knowing Ravana was wrong, he fought loyally for his brother against Rama. He was cursed by Saraswati to sleep for six months at a time.

asuras.name: Andhakasura
asuras.title: The Blind Demon
asuras.desc: A formidable Asura born from the sweat of Lord Shiva.
asuras.details: Blind due to Parvati covering Shiva's eyes playfully, he grew powerful and arrogant. He was ultimately defeated by Shiva and Kali when he tried to abduct Parvati.

asuras.name: Mahishasura
asuras.title: The Buffalo Demon
asuras.desc: A shape-shifting Asura who could take the form of a massive water buffalo.
asuras.details: Protected by a boon that no man or god could kill him, he conquered the heavens. He was ultimately slain by Goddess Durga after a fierce nine-day battle.

asuras.name: Raktabija
asuras.title: The Blood-Seed Demon
asuras.desc: A terrifying Asura whose spilled blood would spawn duplicates of himself.
asuras.details: During battle, every drop of his blood that hit the ground created a new clone. He was finally defeated by Goddess Kali, who drank his blood before it could touch the earth.

asuras.name: Gajamukhasura
asuras.title: The Elephant Demon
asuras.desc: An Asura with the head of an elephant who terrorized the gods.
asuras.details: He was granted a boon that he could not be killed by any weapon. Lord Ganesha defeated him using his own broken tusk, eventually turning the demon into a mouse (his vahana).

asuras.name: Ahiravan
asuras.title: Demon of the Underworld
asuras.desc: A powerful sorcerer and brother of Ravana who ruled Patala (the underworld).
asuras.details: He kidnapped Rama and Lakshmana to sacrifice them to Goddess Kali. Hanuman rescued them by changing his size and slaying Ahiravan in his own realm.

asuras.name: Ravana
asuras.title: Demon King of Lanka
asuras.desc: The ten-headed Rakshasa king of Lanka and primary antagonist of the Ramayana.
asuras.details: A great scholar, devoted follower of Shiva, and master of the Veena, whose arrogance and kidnapping of Sita led to his downfall at the hands of Rama.

asuras.name: Kansa
asuras.title: The Tyrant of Mathura
asuras.desc: The cruel uncle of Lord Krishna who overthrew his own father to claim the throne.
asuras.details: Fearing a prophecy that his sister's eighth child would kill him, he murdered his nephews. He was eventually slain by Krishna, fulfilling the prophecy.

mantra.english: Glory to the Lord of Mathura

asuras.name: Tarakasura
asuras.title: The Invincible Warrior
asuras.desc: A mighty Asura who conquered the universe and drove out the Devas.
asuras.details: He had a boon that he could only be killed by the son of Shiva. This led to the birth of Skanda (Kartikeya), who ultimately led the divine army to defeat him.

asuras.name: Surpanakha
asuras.title: The Demoness of Vengeance
asuras.desc: The sister of Ravana whose actions sparked the great war of Ramayana.
asuras.details: She attempted to seduce Rama and attack Sita, resulting in Lakshmana cutting off her nose. Her desire for revenge caused Ravana to kidnap Sita.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.description: Festival of Lights, celebrating the victory of light over darkness.

festivals.name: Janmashtami
festivals.description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna.

festivals.name: Maha Shivaratri
festivals.description: Night of Shiva, dedicated to Lord Shiva with fasting and night-long vigils.

festivals.name: Navratri
festivals.description: Nine nights dedicated to the goddess Durga and her forms.

festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
festivals.description: Celebrates the birth of Ganesha, the remover of obstacles.
